title: Book One · Chapter 29: We Can Try
story:
On Wednesday morning, Mum takes the boys past Mr Qiu's stall before school.

Ronan carries the kite. Leo carries their page of little down arrows. Mum spoke to Leo's mother about the early walk. The boys ate breakfast at home. Mr Qiu is still eating his bun. He sits behind the pencil jars.

"You are early workers," he says.

"It's class day," Leo tells him.

Mr Qiu wipes his hands. "Then we should look before my tea gets cold."

He doesn't pick the kite up at once. "Does it go up?" he asks. Leo shows the down arrows. "A longer string did not help," Ronan says. The tail helped a little. But the top still points down.

"Good. Your drawings are clear. Your kite goes down."

He means the drawings. Ronan smiles for the first time that morning.

Mr Qiu lifts the kite by its short string. The string is tied near the middle. The top drops forward. He turns it and looks at the strips.

"This line is pulling from one place. We can try two short lines that meet."

"Why two?" Leo asks.

Mr Qiu balances a pencil across one finger. It tips. He changes the place of his finger. Now it rests flat.

"Look at my finger under the pencil. I move my finger, and one end goes down. We can move the string on your kite too. Wind will also push the kite. You still need to try it outside."

He takes a short spare string from his drawer. "This is an old end," he says. "You can use it." Mum nods. Ronan looks at Mr Qiu's string. Mr Qiu gave them this piece. They can use it.

Mr Qiu shows two points on the main stick. The bamboo ends are smooth. The frame is still strong. The boys can keep the same frame.

He ties one small loop while they watch. Then he gives Leo the other end.

"Your hands now."

Leo tries. His knot slides. Ronan holds the stick still. They loosen it and copy the first loop more carefully.

A customer comes for envelopes. Mr Qiu turns to serve her. The boys wait with the kite on the board. Ronan can see the tea cooling beside the half bun.

When Mr Qiu returns, he checks their loops. He ties the two short lines together. They meet in one knot. The boys can move that knot a little. They must mark the knot with a pencil. Then they can move it and try the kite again. "Change one thing first," he says. "Then try the kite. Does it fly better? Write that down."

"Will it fly?" Ronan asks.

"We can try. I cannot promise more than that."

Mum says it is time for school. Mr Qiu gives the bun a disappointed look.

"Another thing that isn't flying today," he says, picking up the cold half.

At the next corner, Ronan stops to look at the kite hanging from its new lines. It sits differently. He can see the new lines clearly. Will the kite fly? They still need to try it.

Leo puts a small pencil mark at the meeting knot. They agree to keep the tail and the string length the same for the next test.

At school, Miss Wu opens the door to let them in with the big brown shape. Jun's green windmill is already on the front table. Ronan puts the kite beside it, leaving a good space between the tail and the turning wheel. The green wheel can turn here. The blue tail has room beside it. Ronan puts the names between the two things. Jun's windmill is on one side. Their kite is on the other.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：balances＝让……保持平衡；loop＝线圈；frame＝框架；test＝试验。

辅助理解：loop＝线圈；frame＝风筝的框架；把两条短线接在一起的knot是绳结。

理解问题：

1. Mr Qiu 看出风筝的哪个问题？
2. 他为什么没有替两个孩子完成整个修理？
